message.content:
I’m not able to pull live data directly from the web, but I can give you an idea of how you might find up‑to‑date information on Los Angeles’ air quality:

| Source | What it offers | How to use it |
|--------|----------------|---------------|
| **AirNow** (EPA) | Real‑time AQI values for specific monitoring stations, plus forecast and health guidance. | Visit https://www.airnow.gov/, enter “Los Angeles” or your ZIP code, and view the latest AQI reading. |
| **OpenAQ** | Aggregated sensor data from many cities worldwide, including Los Angeles. | Go to https://openaq.org/, search for “Los Angeles”, and look at the most recent measurements for PM₂.₅, O₃, NO₂, etc. |
| **City/County dashboards** | Many local agencies publish their own dashboards with station maps and alerts. | Check the City of Los Angeles website or the LA County Department of Public Health site for a dedicated air quality page. |
| **Weather apps** | Apps like Weather.com, AccuWeather, or the built‑in weather app on smartphones often display an AQI icon. | Open your preferred weather app, search for “Los Angeles”, and look for the AQI indicator. |

If you want a quick snapshot without navigating, you could also try a voice assistant (e.g., “Hey Siri, what’s the air quality in Los Angeles?”) or ask a smart speaker.

Let me know if you’d like help interpreting the numbers once you’ve got them!
message.reasoning: The user asks about current air quality in Los Angeles. We need real-time data. We don't have direct API access. We can provide general info and suggest checking AirNow or local sources.
